title: Power Automate: export work queue items to CSV from the automation center
summary: Hold: the briefing treats Dataverse request accounting as undocumented even though Microsoft's platform rule covers reads from any client, including user-driven operations. Its categorical statement that Dataverse controls do not follow the downloaded CSV also lacks evidence for this export; the roadmap facts and both documented control paths check out.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: Direct user security roles are managed in Power Platform admin center under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Users > user > Manage security roles.
claims.quote:
In the Manage pane, select Environments, and then select an environment from the list.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The documented role-assignment call is POST [Organization URI]/api/data/v9.0/systemusers(azureactivedirectoryobjectid=<user object ID>)/systemuserroles_association/$ref with the roles reference in @odata.id.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: The API source describes assigning a security role to a Microsoft Entra ID group user.
claims.quote: An administrator can assign a security role to a Microsoft Entra ID group user. If the user doesn't exist in Dataverse, the system automatically adds the user when you assign the role directly to the user.

claims.where: controls[1]; summary; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: No tenant or environment switch to turn this CSV export on or off is documented in either the UI or an API.
claims.quote: Searched: "work queue" "CSV" "disable" "Power Platform admin center"; "work queue" "export" "pac" "Power Platform API" setting; "work queue" "export" "PowerShell" "setting". Opened automation-center-overview, work-queues-manage and work-queues-known-limitations.

claims.claim: Assigning security roles requires at least Read and Assign privileges on the Security Role table.
claims.quote: To assign security roles to a user, you need to have the appropriate privileges (minimum privileges are Read and Assign on the Security Role table).

claims.claim: System Administrator has the required security-role assignment privileges by default.
claims.quote: By default, the System Administrator security role has all the required privileges to assign security roles to any user, including assigning the System Administrator security role.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents Dataverse RBAC for limiting work queue use in API-based scenarios.
claims.quote: if you want to limit the use of work queues in cloud flow and API-based scenarios, you should use Dataverse RBAC to control access to the underlying tables.

claims.claim: Restricting access to work queue tables limits which work queue data users can see in the automation center.
claims.quote: Additionally, administrators can create custom security roles with row-level privileges to control the data users can view and interact with.

claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits the briefing's description of a launched, automatically enabled change with medium risk and an access-control decision.
claims.quote: status: "launched"; risk: "medium"; defaultState: "on"; action: "prepare". The body says an administrator who does nothing should expect users to start downloading and recommends reviewing access.
claims.fix: Change action from 'prepare' to 'act-now': the change is already launched, reaches its audience automatically and requires the access and file-handling decisions described in the briefing.
